why: The prompt now avoids cutting inside verbal complexes (C4) so predicates and their punctuation tend to stay intact—helpful for long-latency examples—but the new C3 rule for splitting multi-token spans was applied too broadly, causing over‑splitting (even into single characters) and isolating punctuation/quotes; that fragmentation shows up as losses in the ≤5 and ≤7 bins despite gains at very short (≤3) and very long (≤99) latencies.
lesson: Narrow the multi-token-splitting rule so it only splits true multi-token names when necessary and never breaks ordinary words or isolates punctuation/quotes; keep the verbal-complex protection but avoid applying splitting heuristics that fragment short/medium pieces.
